issues.legal_issue: A first appellate court's order setting aside a decree made on the merits and directing a fresh trial is a remand under the rule governing retrials and is appealable when the statutory conditions for an appeal from that remand are met.
material_facts: The trial court disposed of the suit on its merits and granted permanent injunction.
The first appellate court set aside that decree and directed the trial court to decide the suit afresh after allowing both parties to lead oral and documentary evidence.
The appellants challenged the first appellate court's remand order.
issues.conclusion: The first appellate court acted under Order 41 Rule 23A, and its remand order was appealable under Order 43 Rule 1(u).
issues.legal_principle: Order 41 Rule 23 applies when a suit was disposed of on a preliminary point and that decree is reversed. Order 41 Rule 23A permits remand when a case disposed of otherwise than on a preliminary point is reversed and a retrial is considered necessary. Under Order 41 Rule 25, the appellate court remains seised of the matter and refers an omitted issue or factual question to the trial court for findings. An order under Rule 23A is appealable under Order 43 Rule 1(u) when an appeal would lie from the appellate decree.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_appellate_remand_order and trial_court_decided_case_on_merits and appellate_court_reversed_decree and remand_directs_fresh_trial

predicates.appeal_challenges_appellate_remand_order: A party brought an appeal challenging an order by an appellate court that remanded a case.
predicates.trial_court_decided_case_on_merits: The trial court resolved the case on its merits rather than disposing of it on a preliminary point.
predicates.appellate_court_reversed_decree: The appellate court set aside the trial court's decree.
predicates.remand_directs_fresh_trial: The appellate court directed the trial court to decide the case afresh after a retrial.

issues.definition: When a party appeals an appellate remand order following a merits decision that was reversed and a fresh trial was directed, the remand order is appealable.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal from an appealable remand order is maintainable even though its hearing is confined to the grounds available in a second appeal.
material_facts: The appellants filed a civil miscellaneous appeal against the remand order under Order 43 Rule 1(u).
The High Court dismissed that appeal as not maintainable, relying on Narayanan v. Kumaran & Ors.
The High Court treated the limits on the grounds available in such an appeal as a bar to its maintainability.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in holding the appeal not maintainable. An appeal under Order 43 Rule 1(u) is maintainable, but it may be heard only on the grounds available in a second appeal under Section 100; the civil miscellaneous appeal was restored for hearing and disposal according to law.
issues.legal_principle: Order 43 Rule 1(u), read with Section 104, provides for an appeal from specified remand orders where an appeal would lie from the appellate decree. Narayanan v. Kumaran & Ors. (2004) 4 SCC 26 holds that such an appeal is confined to the grounds enumerated in Section 100. That restriction concerns the scope of hearing, not maintainability; the two concepts must be distinguished.

predicates.appeal_challenges_appealable_remand_orde: A party brought an appeal challenging a remand order of a kind for which an appeal is available.
predicates.underlying_appellate_decree_is_appealabl: An appeal would lie from the decree of the appellate court that made the remand order.

issues.definition: An appeal challenging an appealable remand order is maintainable, but its hearing is limited to the grounds available in a second appeal.
